README 節錄：# Relax > [!WARNING] > **Experimental.** Relax is for development iteration: running, testing and live-editing your program while you work on it. Build anything you release with Rust itself: `cargo build --release` with rustc. So far it has been tested mostly in Makepad's own edit-run loop and only lightly on other projects, so expect rough edges elsewhere and please report them. ### Rust without the wait. **rustc builds your program, then you run it. Docs · Deploy · Migrate · Bindings · Examples · Discord ## What is OpenOrange OpenOrange runs your existing Cloudflare Workers project on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or your own servers, with no changes to your code. title: paulirish/chrome-capture
body:
60-120fps / 2160p tab video/audio capture from Chrome

README 節錄：# chrome-capture Record a Chrome tab at 60-120fps (up to 2160p) straight to a AV1 `.mp4`. Tab audio too. No ffmpeg. ```bash npx chrome-capture https://paulirish.github.io/chrome-capture/ demo.mp4 4s ``` ## Chrome 153+ has a native MP4 tab recorder! 😻 For the past ~decade, `Page.startScreencast` was the only way to get video frames out of CDP. That API is from ~2013, built so DevTools could show a live preview of a USB-tethered Android. (So good!) Both Playwright (`recordVideo`) and Puppeteer (`page.screencast()`) built their video capture on top of it: Chrome JPEG-encodes each frame, base64s it into JSON over CDP, waits for an ack, and the library pipes those JPEGs into `ffmpeg`. It's served us well. In Sept 2026… the new `Page.startScreenRecording` landed (thx alex rudenko!). Frames go **straight from the compositor** to an out-of-process encoder over shared memory, and Chrome **writes AV1 into the mp4** as it goes (plus optional tab audio). 💅 Stopping is ~instant because the encoding is already done (no multi-second `ffmpeg` flush at the end). And you can start/stop recording whenever you want: log in, warm up the page, then record just the interaction. **In short: It's hot.
